entities.name: Chlothar III
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Chlothar III, King of the Franks, reigned over Neustria and Burgundy from 657 CE until his death in 673 CE, briefly holding Austrasia as well. Born around 650 CE, he was a pivotal figure in the accelerating decline of Merovingian royal authority, a process often termed the 'rois fainéants' (do-nothing kings) era. His reign, largely controlled by powerful regents and Mayors of the Palace, particularly Ebroin of Neustria, underscores the gradual shift of effective power from the monarch to the aristocratic magnates, setting the stage for the eventual Carolingian takeover.

His ascension to the throne of Neustria and Burgundy at the tender age of seven, following the death of his father Clovis II, immediately placed him under the regency of his mother, Balthild. This period saw the formidable rise of Ebroin, Mayor of the Palace, who consolidated significant power by centralizing administration and suppressing rival aristocratic factions. In 662 CE, Chlothar briefly reunited the Frankish realms by inheriting Austrasia upon the death of his uncle, Childebert the Adopted, but this union was short-lived, as Austrasian nobles soon demanded their own king, leading to the enthronement of Chlothar's brother Childeric II. Throughout his reign, Chlothar III remained largely a figurehead, with Ebroin dictating policy, including the important Synod of Autun in 663 CE, which aimed to reform the Frankish church and reinforce episcopal authority loyal to the Mayor.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Chlothar III's reign, though largely controlled by powerful regents, significantly accelerated the decline of Merovingian royal authority and solidified the power base of the Mayors of the Palace, a crucial step toward the Carolingian ascendancy.
